column1: Case Pack value from Product Specs does not propagate to the Distributor Sales Report
column29:
The Case Pack value set on a Product Specification does not appear in the Distributor Sales Report. The field shows blank/null in the report output even when Case Pack is populated on the source product spec.

*Expected behavior*

When a Case Pack value exists on a Product Specification, that value should flow through to the Distributor Sales Report for the corresponding product line.

*Actual behavior*

Case Pack in the Distributor Sales Report is empty/null regardless of the value set on Product Specs.

*Steps to reproduce*

* Open a Product Specification record with a Case Pack value set.
* Generate/view the Distributor Sales Report for the same product.
* Observe that Case Pack is missing or null in the report.

*Scope*

* Distributor Sales Report only. Monthly Report is out of scope unless investigation indicates otherwise.
* Investigate the propagation path: Product Specs to report generation pipeline. Likely candidates: field not included in report query/DTO, mapping gap in the report service, or field not joined/persisted correctly at report build time.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Root cause of the missing propagation is identified and documented.
* Case Pack value correctly appears in the Distributor Sales Report, matching the source Product Spec value.
* Fix verified against existing report records, not just newly generated ones.
* Confirm whether a backfill is required for already-generated reports.

column1: Add a admin read API to test the read access of the given database

*Summary*

Add an admin-only read API endpoint to verify read access to a given external database connection.

Context

We need a way to confirm that Caboodle can establish a connection and read from an external SQL Server database before wiring up any downstream ingestion/mapping work. This endpoint acts as a connectivity and read-access smoke test.

Target Database (Bubbies)

* Host: 20.245.139.43
* Port: 1433
* Database: BUBBI
* Table: dbo.ForecastData
* Credentials: Stored in secrets manager under <KEY_NAME>. Do not hardcode or commit.

*Requirements*

* Add a new admin-only endpoint (RBAC: admin role required).
* Endpoint attempts to connect to the configured SQL Server instance using stored credentials.
* Perform a lightweight read against dbo.ForecastData (e.g. SELECT TOP 1 or row count) to confirm read access.
* Return a structured result: connection status, read status, row count or sample metadata on success, sanitized error message on failure.
* Handle failure cases gracefully: unreachable host, auth failure, missing table, timeout.
* Apply a sensible connection/query timeout.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* Endpoint exists and is protected behind admin RBAC.
* Successful call against BUBBI / dbo.ForecastData returns a success response with read confirmation.
* Auth failure, unreachable host, and missing-table cases return clear, sanitized error responses.
* Credentials are read from configuration/secrets, not hardcoded.
* No credentials or connection strings appear in logs or API responses.

*Notes*

* Connection details verified manually before implementation.
* Scope is read-only verification — no writes, no schema changes.

column1: User-Managemet: Replace Role-Specific Invite Email Templates with a Shared Template
column29:
Today, when a user is invited to the platform, the invitation email is rendered from a *role-specific template* — a separate template per user type (Brand Sub-User, Broker Sub-User, User, Broker, Brand Owner). These templates have drifted apart in copy, branding, and structure, and every content/brand change has to be duplicated across all of them, which is error-prone and slows delivery.

This ticket consolidates all role-specific invite email templates into a *single shared invitation template* that is used for every invited user type, with any genuinely role-dependent content (e.g. a role label or CTA text) driven by parameters/placeholders rather than by maintaining separate templates.

h2. Current Behavior

* Each user type has its own invite email template.
* User types (see {{UserTypes}} enum): {{BrandSubUser (1)}}, {{BrokerSubUser (2)}}, {{User (3)}}, {{Broker (4)}}, {{BrandOwner (5)}}.
* The admin portal triggers invites via the invite endpoint sending {{{ email, userType }}}; template selection happens server-side based on {{userType}}.
* Copy/branding fixes must be made in every template separately.

h2. Desired Behavior

* A *single shared invite email template* is used for all invited users regardless of role.
* Any role-specific text is injected via template variables/placeholders (not separate templates).
* Invitation link, expiry, and inviter details continue to work exactly as before.
* Removing the per-role templates causes no regression in the invite flow for any user type.

h2. Scope

*In scope*

* Introduce/define the single shared invite email template.
* Point invite email sending for all user types to the shared template.
* Parameterize any legitimately role-dependent content.
* Deprecate/remove the now-unused role-specific templates.

*Out of scope*

* Non-invite transactional emails (password reset, notifications, etc.).

h2. Acceptance Criteria

# Inviting a user of *each* user type (BrandSubUser, BrokerSubUser, User, Broker, BrandOwner) produces an email rendered from the *same shared template*.
# Role-dependent content, if any, renders correctly per user type via placeholders.
# The invitation link is valid, respects expiry, and completes the existing accept-invite flow for every user type.
# Inviter and any dynamic fields (email, brand association, expiry) render correctly.
# The legacy role-specific templates are no longer referenced by the invite flow (and are removed or clearly deprecated).

h2. Testing / QA

* Send a test invite for all five user types; verify each uses the shared template and renders correctly.
* Verify accept-invite works end-to-end per role.
* Verify placeholders (role label, name, brand, link, expiry) populate correctly and there are no empty/broken merge fields.

column1: Setup & Develop SNS Webhook to Receive Email Sending Events
column29:
Implement an SNS webhook endpoint to receive email delivery events from the email provider (e.g., AWS SES via SNS). The primary goal is to track the status of outbound emails and detect failures for critical emails such as login authentication emails, password reset emails, and other system-generated notifications.

The webhook should securely receive and process SNS notifications, allowing the system to log and monitor email delivery outcomes for troubleshooting and operational visibility.

*Acceptance Criteria:*

* Create a webhook endpoint to receive SNS notifications.
* Validate and securely process incoming SNS messages.
* Handle SNS subscription confirmation requests.
* Process relevant email sending events, including but not limited to:
** Delivery
** Bounce
** Complaint
** Reject
** Delivery delay (if applicable)
* Persist or log email event details for monitoring and debugging.
* Ensure failed email events can be correlated with the original email request (where possible).
* Add appropriate error handling and logging for invalid or failed webhook requests.
* Document the webhook endpoint, expected payloads, and configuration steps.

*Business Value:*

This implementation will provide visibility into email delivery failures, enabling the team to quickly identify issues affecting critical emails (such as login authentication emails) and improve the reliability and observability of the email delivery pipeline.

column1: [BE] Email log API with single & bulk resend
column29:
Provide the backend to support the admin Sent Emails feature: a paginated list of all emails sent from the system, plus endpoints to resend one or multiple emails.

Emails are logged at send time (recipient, subject, type/category, body/template reference, timestamp, status). Resend re-dispatches using the stored email content and original recipient.

*Acceptance Criteria:*

* Sent emails are persisted with: recipient, subject, email type/category, body or template reference, sent timestamp, and status (Sent / Failed).
* {{GET}}-equivalent list endpoint returns sent emails, paginated, newest first. Follow the existing POST-list + filter-options pattern used elsewhere in admin.
* List response includes all fields needed for the FE table (recipient, subject, type, sent date/time, status).
* Resend endpoint accepts a single email log ID and re-dispatches using stored content/recipient.
* Bulk resend endpoint accepts an array of email log IDs and re-dispatches each; returns a per-item result (success/failure) rather than failing the whole batch on one error.
* Resend creates a new sent-email log entry (or updates status) so history stays accurate — grooming to confirm which.
* Clean architecture: separate controller / service / repository; no business logic in controller.

*Open questions:*

* Resend as new log row vs. status update on original?
* Bulk batch size cap / async job (poll pattern) vs. synchronous?
* Filters exposed on list (recipient, date range, status, type)?

column1: Broker Dashboard | Category Review Propagation
column29:
h2. Description:

We need to implement the backend propagation and visibility logic for the *Category Review List* based on who performs the upload or addition. The goal is to ensure proper data distribution from Brokers down to Brands, while keeping Brand-specific uploads isolated—unless they are explicitly committed to a shared calendar.

h3. Core User Stories:

# *As a Broker*, when I upload/add a Category Review list, I want it to automatically propagate to all Brand environments associated with my account, saving me from manual duplication.
# *As a Brand*, when I upload/add a Category Review list, I want it to remain private to my environment so it does not clutter the Broker's dashboard or other brands' views.
# *As a Brand*, when I assign an item from my review list to my *Category Review Calendar*, I want that specific calendar event to push up to the *Broker Master Category Review Calendar* (once created).

h2. Technical Functional Requirements

h3. 1. Broker-Level Uploads (Top-Down Propagation)

* *Trigger:* A user with a {{Broker}} role uploads or adds a Category Review list.
* *Behavior:* The system must identify all {{Brand}} IDs/environments associated with that Broker's account and instantly propagate/copy the list to those environments.
* *Visibility:* Visible in the Broker Dashboard and all associated Brand Dashboards.

h3. 2. Brand-Level Uploads (Isolated Environment)

* *Trigger:* A user with a {{Brand}} role uploads or adds a Category Review list.
* *Behavior:* The data must remain strictly within that specific Brand's database schema/environment.
* *Visibility:* Visible *only* to that Brand. It must *not* propagate to the Broker Dashboard or any sister brands.

h3. 3. Brand Calendar Event Promotion (Bottom-Up Exception)

* *Trigger:* A Brand user takes an item from their local category review list and adds it to their local *Category Review Calendar*.
* *Behavior:*
** The list item itself remains isolated to the brand.
** _However_, the calendar assignment must trigger an event pipeline to propagate this specific date/category combo up to the upcoming *Broker Master Category Review Calendar* feature space.
** _Dev Note:_ Ensure the data structure for local brand calendars is ready to feed a master broker view once the master calendar UI is officially built.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

{noformat}Gherkin{noformat}

{noformat}Scenario: A Broker uploads a category list
  Given a Broker is logged into the Broker Dashboard
  When the Broker uploads a new Category Review list
  Then the list should be visible to the Broker
  And the list must be immediately propagated and visible in all associated Brand environments

Scenario: A Brand uploads a category list
  Given a Brand user is logged into their dashboard
  When the Brand user uploads a new Category Review list
  Then the list should only be visible within that specific Brand's environment
  And the list must NOT be visible on the Broker Dashboard or any other Brand Dashboards

Scenario: A Brand adds a list item to their Calendar
  Given a Brand has a localized Category Review list
  When the Brand maps a list item to their Category Review Calendar
  Then that calendar entry must be flagged/staged to sync with the Broker Master Category Review Calendar pipeline
{noformat}

h2. UX/UI Notes:

* *Broker view:* Needs a visual indicator or column showing that an item was "Propagated to All Brands."
* *Brand view:* Should clearly differentiate between list items that were pushed down by their Broker (read-only or editable depending on current permissions) vs. items they added locally themselves.

column1: Product Specs & Distributor Report KEHE Master Pack Issue
column29:
h2. *Summary*

*Bug:* Distributor Report calculation error when KeHE Pack Size and Unit of Sale (UOS) do not match (e.g., Viori Beauty)

h2. *Description*

We have identified a calculation bug in the Distributor Report inside Caboodle.

h3. *Context*

* Caboodle pulls KeHE sales reports, which report in *eaches* (unit volume).
* To calculate sales in *case volume*, Caboodle divides the units sold by the case pack size defined in the *Product Spec Module*.
* *The Normal Case (95% of the time):* KeHE Pack Size and UOS match perfectly (e.g., Sunshine Nuts: Pack Size = 6, UOS = 6, Ratio = 1). The report calculates correctly.
* *The Edge Case (Small % of brands, mostly Health & Beauty):* Pack Size and UOS _do not_ match because Viori sells to KeHE in Case Packs of 36, but KeHE sells to Retailers in Case Packs of 3. This mismatch is causing an inflated calculation (multiplying data by a factor of 12 instead of 1), leading to errors in the Distributor Report.

h2. *Example Case Study for Debugging*

* *Broker:* Noble Sales
* *Brand:* Viori Beauty
* *Product:* Bar Aged Sandalwood Conditioner Bar
* *UPC:* {{197644130573}}

h3. *Data Breakdown:*

* *KeHE Brand Item Location Report:* Pack Size = *36* (Column O) | UOS = *3* (Column Q)
* *KeHE POD Report:* Current Quantity (Units Sold to Retailer) = *3* (Column AM) | Price = *$15.84*
* *Current Caboodle Setup:* Product Spec Module case pack is currently set to *3*.

h3. *The Bug in Action:*

Because of the UOS/Pack Size mismatch, the Distributor Report dollar sales for Viori are not matching column AO in the POD report. There is an incorrect multiplier occurring.

{quote}*Testing Note:* I tried manually changing this item’s case pack to *36* in the Caboodle Product Spec Module to test a fix, but the change *did not reflect or update* in the Distributor Report.{quote}

Additionally, on the Distributor Report for this Viori item (filtered by _KeHE > Sprouts > Aged_), dollar sales appear for all months, but cases shipped *only show data for January*.

h2. *Expected Behavior*

# The Distributor Report should correctly calculate case volume and dollar sales even when a brand's KeHE Pack Size and UOS differ.
# Changes made to the case pack configuration in the Product Spec Module should dynamically update or trigger a recalculation on the Distributor Report.
# Cases shipped should consistently display across all months where sales dollars exist.

h2. *Steps to Reproduce / Verify*

# Open the Distributor Report and filter by *KeHE > Sprouts > Aged Sandalwood Conditioner Bar* to view the Viori item.
# Review the attached data files to compare the logic of a working brand (*Sunshine Nuts*) vs. a broken brand (*Viori Beauty*).

* [ ] {{Sunshine Nuts - KeHE POD Report}} (Calculations match perfectly)
* [ ] {{Viori - KeHE Brand Item Location Report}} (See columns O & Q for mismatch)
* [ ] {{Viori - KeHE POD Report}} (See column AT for user-added calculation demonstrating the error)
* [ ] {{Distributor_Report_Viori_Screenshot.png}} (Showing missing case data after Jan)

column1: Distributor Report | Velocity Calculations Need Review
column29:
h2. Issue Type:

* Bug / Functional Investigation > Bijoy and CW discovered the issue. The Distributor report Velocity Report is calculating by cases and not units. The Calculation needs to be updated from Cases to Units to report the Velocity correctly. 

h2. Description:

A discrepancy has been identified in the *Velocity Report* calculation for *Units Per Store Per Week (UPSPW)*. The dashboard currently displays a value of *0.09*, whereas the raw filtered data calculates out to *0.61*.

There is a strong suspicion that the "Weeks" variable in the backend calculation is hardcoded to a fixed timeframe (e.g., 52 weeks) instead of dynamically adjusting to the user's active date filter (Jan–May = 20 weeks).

h3. Steps to Reproduce / Environment Context:

# *Path:* Broker Noble Sales Brand  Miracle Noodles > Item: _Angel Hair_ | Case Pack Size: _6_
# *Report Page:* Go to *Distributor Report* and filter by *KeHE* and Product *Angel Hair*.
# *Target Location:* Scroll to the *Velocity Report* at the very bottom of the page.

h3. Data Points Checked:

* *Sales Quantity (Cases*Packs):* 117
* *Pack Size:* 6
* *Total Calculated Units:* 117 *  6 = 702 units
* *Active Filter Date Range:* January to May (~20 weeks)
* *Active Store Count:* 58 stores

h3. Expected Backend Formula vs. Actual UI Output:

* *Expected Logic (Dynamic Weeks):*
The calculation is Units/weeks/stores = 702/20/58 = .61
* *Actual UI Display:* *0.09*

h2. Developer Investigation Requirements:

# *Verify the "Weeks" Variable Logic:*
#* Review the backend calculation for {{Units Per Store Per Week}} on the Velocity Report.
#* Does the week denominator dynamically scale based on the user's active date filter (e.g., recognizing 8 weeks if filtering only Jan-Feb, or 20 weeks for Jan-May)?
#* _Note:_ If it is currently hardcoded to 52 weeks, it is still not matching the *0.09* on the screen. Please trace exactly where the current denominator is pulling its week and store counts from.
# *Verify Pack Size Multiplier:*
#* Ensure that {{Sales Quantity}} is properly multiplying by the item's {{Pack Size}} (6) to arrive at true _Units_ before running the velocity division. If the system is calculating using raw quantity packages instead of individual units ($\frac{117}{20 \times 58} = \mathbf{0.10}$), this gets incredibly close to the broken 0.09 value.
# *Implement Fix:*
#* Ensure both the active store count and the active date filter duration dynamically feed the velocity denominator.

h2. Acceptance Criteria:

* The Velocity Report at the bottom of the Distributor page must display mathematically accurate UPSPW metrics reflecting any applied date and distributor filters.

column1: Data Mapping | Unmapped Store List
column29:
*Objective:* Eliminate the manual overhead of repetitive store mapping by implementing an automated *Entity Resolution (ER) Service* within the data ingestion pipeline. We need to move from 1-to-1 manual mapping to a confidence-score-based automated matching system.

h3. 1. Problem Statement

Current architecture requires individual manual mapping for every store entry. This is non-scalable:

* *Volume:* 12,000+ unique stores identified for only 9 brands (Jan–May 2026).
* *Redundancy:* Retailers like Sprouts (500+ locations) are currently re-mapped for every variation of their listing, resulting in up to 2,500 redundant manual inputs per retailer.
* *Operational Risk:* Dependencies in Distributor and Monthly Reports are currently bottlenecked, leading to data inaccuracy and reporting delays.

h3. 2. Proposed Technical Solution: Automated Entity Resolution

We need to shift from "Manual Mapping" to an "Automated Matching with Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)" workflow.

h4. A. The Matching Engine

Implement a fuzzy matching algorithm that calculates a *Similarity Score (0–100%)* based on weighted attributes:

* *Primary Weight (High):* Store Number, Retailer Name, Zip Code.
* *Secondary Weight (Medium):* Normalized Street Name, City.
* *Tertiary Weight (Low):* Geo-coordinates (Lat/Long).

*Logic Flow:*

# *Ingestion:* New store record arrives.
# *ER Service:* System compares new record against existing "Master Store List."
# *Thresholding:*
#* *Score > 95%:* Auto-map and link to existing Master ID.
#* *Score 75%–95%:* Flag for "Supervisor Approval" queue (fast-track UI).
#* *Score < 75%:* Require manual entry/creation of new store entity.

h4. B. Normalization Pre-Processing

Before the matching engine runs, we must implement a *Standardization Layer* to handle variations (e.g., "Sprouts 107 Murphy" vs. "Sprouts #107 - Murphy St").

* *Regex/Tokenization:* Strip common suffixes/prefixes (e.g., "Store", "#", "St", "Rd").
* *Key-Value Extraction:* Extract {{Retailer_Name}} and {{Store_Number}} as discrete fields to anchor the matching logic.

h3. 3. Implementation Requirements for Engineering

* *Architecture:* Define a service (or AWS Glue/Lambda function) that intercepts the "CRM Data Upload" flow _before_ it hits the mapping UI.
* *Feedback Loop:* Ensure the "Supervisor Approval" queue allows for batch-approving items flagged by the ER service.
* *UI/UX:* Add a column in the mapping interface displaying the "Confidence Score" and "Suggested Match" to allow for quick verification.

h3. 4. Strategic Discussion: Auto-Population

You mentioned the idea of auto-populating the store list from the data sync.

* *Recommendation:* Proceed with this, but *only* if it feeds into the new Entity Resolution service rather than the legacy manual mapping screen. The data sync should create a "Proposed Entity," which the ER service then attempts to resolve.

*Next Steps for the Team:*

# *Define the Weights:* Are we in agreement that {{Store Number}} and {{Retailer}} should hold the highest weight in our similarity algorithm?
# *Threshold Setting:* Should we start with a conservative threshold (e.g., 98%) to ensure no false positives, and lower it as the model matures?
# *Audit:* Can the dev team pull a sample of 100 Sprouts entries to run a pilot test of this scoring logic?
# Question: Regarding the KeHE Data, I noticed that we might be pulling in sales data that might not be relevant to the current year. Let’s discuss what is getting pulled in. For example See image below, were we are mapping records from last year’s sales data. 



# SPROUTS/MPC 107 MURPHY BAKE 
# SPROUTS 107-MURPHY-FROZ 
# SPROUTS FARMERS MARKET 107 
# SPROUTS 107-MURPHY-GROC 
# SPROUTS 107-MURPHY-FROZ PROM 



For Sprouts 651 information is from Prior Year, with 0 for Current Year. By pulling in this information we’re manually mapping data that may be irrelevant. Let’s review exactly what information is getting pulled into the system and see if we an parse out what’s not needed to reduce the load.

column1: [FE] Distributor Sales Report | Import functionality
column29:
This feature lets users import *Distributor Sales Reports* (KeHE or UNFI) into Caboodle by uploading a CSV file and tagging it with the reporting period it belongs to.

----

h4. What the user can do

* Upload a distributor sales report CSV file (KeHE or UNFI).
* Select which *distributor* the file is from (KeHE or UNFI).
* Select the *month* and *year* the report covers.
* Start the import and watch progress in real time.
* See whether the import succeeded or failed, and download a list of failed rows if there were any.

----

h4. How the flow works (user perspective)

# User opens the *Distributor Sales Reports* import screen.
# User picks a *CSV file* from their computer.
# User selects:
#* *Distributor* — KeHE or UNFI
#* *Month* — January through December
#* *Year* — any year between 1900 and 2100
# User clicks *Start Import*.
# The file uploads with a visible progress bar.
# Once uploaded, the system begins processing the report.
# The screen shows live progress: how many rows have been processed, how many succeeded, how many failed.
# When finished:
#* *Success* → user sees a summary of the import.
#* *Failure* → user sees an error message and, if available, a link to download a file listing the rows that failed.

----

h4. Acceptance criteria

* The import screen has fields for *file*, *distributor*, *month*, and *year*.
* Only {{.csv}} files can be selected. Other file types are rejected with a clear message.
* *Distributor* options are limited to *KeHE* and *UNFI*.
* *Month* options are *January through December*.
* *Year* accepts values between *1900 and 2100*, and defaults to the current year.
* The *Start Import* button stays disabled until all four fields are filled.
* A progress bar is shown while the file is uploading.
* Once upload finishes, processing begins automatically.
* During processing, the user can see:
** Current status (uploading / processing / completed / failed)
** Progress percentage
** Number of rows processed
** Number of successful rows
** Number of failed rows
* When the import *completes successfully*, the user sees a clear success state and can start a new import.
* When the import *fails*, the user sees the error message and, if available, a *Download error file* link.
* If the user tries to leave the page while uploading, they are asked to confirm.
* The month and year picked by the user determine which reporting period the data belongs to — the system does *not* read the period from inside the CSV file.

column1: [FE] Distributor Report Refresh

Add a refresh button to the Distributor Report page that re-fetches data for all reports/widgets on the page in a single action, without requiring a full page reload or manual filter re-application.

* Clicking the button re-fetches data for *all reports/widgets* rendered on the page (5+ reports) using the *currently applied filters*.

* Each report should show its existing loading state during the refresh.
* The refresh button itself should:
** Show a loading/spinning state while any report is still fetching.
** Be disabled during the refresh to prevent duplicate triggers.
** Re-enable once all reports complete (success or error).
* Filter values, pagination, sorting, and other UI state must be preserved — refresh only re-runs the data fetches, it does not reset the page.

h4. Acceptance Criteria

* Refresh button visible next to filters on the Distributor Report page.
* Clicking refresh triggers data re-fetch for every report on the page.
* All reports refresh in parallel.
* Currently applied filters are respected during refresh.
* Button shows loading state while refresh is in progress.
* Button is disabled during refresh and re-enables on completion.
* UI state (filters, pagination, sort, scroll) is preserved across refresh.
* Individual report loading indicators behave normally during refresh.
* Works consistently across supported browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox).

column136:
09/Jul/26 10:51 AM;712020:c7e0341d-5b2c-4fbd-9069-516ecf5d2014;Instead of implementing a separate "remove role" option or disabling the assignment button as originally suggested, we overhauled the backend architecture to support *seamless, atomic role transitions*. The {{AssignRoleAsync}} endpoint has been refactored to natively handle users who already have an active role by performing a complete "handover" process in a single transaction. When an admin assigns a new role to an existing user, the system now automatically:

# Validates the transition and ensures a designated "Replacement User" is provided if the user is vacating a critical role (like {{BrandOwner}} or {{Broker}}).
# Safely transfers all existing assets (such as assigned Brands and child users in the hierarchy) to the replacement user to prevent orphaned records.
# Cleans up any outdated role context (e.g., removing old sub-user connections).
# Swaps the Identity roles and provisions the new role's context (linking new brands and hierarchy positions).
# Invalidates active sessions for both users so new security permissions take effect instantly.

This approach completely eliminates the friction of requiring a manual "remove role" step. It turns role assignment into an intelligent, one-click promotion/demotion workflow that guarantees strict data integrity and a much smoother user experience.

column1: User Managemnet | Invitation Registration Link Redirects Logged-In Users to Login Page Instead of Signup Page
column29:
If a user is already signed in to the system and then clicks on a new invitation/registration email link, the system redirects the user to the login page instead of taking them to the signup/registration flow associated with the invitation.

This breaks the expected invitation onboarding flow and creates confusion for users who are already authenticated.

h3. Steps to Reproduce

# Log in to the system with any existing account
# Receive a new invitation/registration email
# Click the invitation registration link while still logged in

h3. Actual Behavior

The invitation link redirects the user to the login page.

h3. Expected Behavior

The invitation link should:

* Open the intended signup/registration page
* Validate the invitation token properly
* Allow the user to continue the invitation flow

Possible expected handling:

* If the logged-in user matches the invited email → continue registration flow
* If the logged-in user is different from the invited email → show a proper warning/message and request account switch/logout if necessary

Example message:

{quote}“You are currently logged in with a different account. Please log out and continue with the invited email account.”{quote}

column1: User Managemnet | Prevent Multiple Pending Invitations for the Same Brand Owner Role
column29:
Currently, a single brand can have only one owner user.

During the *Invite User* flow, brands are shown as disabled only when an invited user has already accepted the invitation and become associated with the brand.

Because of this behavior, multiple pending invitations can be sent for the same brand if the first invited user has not yet accepted the invitation.

As a result:

* Admin can invite multiple users for the same brand owner role
* The first user who accepts the invitation gets registered successfully
* Subsequent users encounter an error during registration/signup because the brand already has an owner

This creates a confusing and inconsistent user experience.

h3. Possible Solutions

h4. Option 1 (Recommended)

When an invitation is created for a brand owner:

* Mark the selected brand as *reserved*
* Disable that brand for future owner invitations until:
** the invitation expires
** invitation is cancelled
** invitation is rejected
** or the invited user completes registration

This prevents duplicate pending invitations at the source.

h4. Option 2

Allow multiple invitations but validate during resend/signup flow:

* Before registration completion, check whether the brand already has:
** an active owner
** or another accepted invitation
* Show a proper message such as:

{quote}“This brand already has an assigned owner. Your invitation is no longer valid.”{quote}

This improves UX but still allows conflicting pending invites.

column29:
*User Story*
*As a* Broker, *I want* Promo Management to show only promotions the brand has pushed to Approved, *So that* I don't see or act on sandboxed promotions.

*Acceptance Criteria*
*Scenario:*
    Given a brand has a promotion in Trade Spend Sandbox
    And the brand has pushed that promotion to Approved (i.e. it now exists as a live TradeSpendPromo linked via SandboxPromotionID)
    When I open the Promotional Management view
    Then the promotion is displayed in the list

*Scenario:*
    Given a brand has a promotion in Trade Spend Sandbox
    And the brand has NOT pushed that promotion to Approved
    When I open the Promotional Management view
    Then the promotion is NOT displayed in the list

*Scenario:*
    Given I am assigned to multiple brands
    And each brand has a mix of Sandbox-only promotions and promotions pushed to Approved
    When I open the Promotional Management view
    Then only the promotions pushed to Approved, from my assigned brands, are displayed
    And no Sandbox-only promotions from any assigned brand appear in the list

*Scenario:*
    Given a promotion was previously pushed to Approved and is visible in Promo Management
    And the brand edits the promotion in Sandbox and pushes it to Approved again
    When I open the Promotional Management view
    Then the promotion is still displayed, reflecting the updated pushed data

*Scenario:*
    Given the Promotional Management list is showing only promotions pushed to Approved
    When I apply a filter (e.g. year, retailer, banner, category, distributor)
    Then only Approved promotions matching the filter are shown

WFM PM Fee

The Goal is to allow the user to enter the fees that are associated with Whole Foods Amazon Prime which are applied to every Promotion. They are unique in how they are calculated. ·       See sample WFM Planner Attached. In column AC (Total PRIME Redemption (Dollars)) you can see the calculation.

column1: [BE] Combine KeHE and UNFI Distributor Reports into a Unified Report
column29:
Currently, KeHE and UNFI distributor reports are implemented separately despite sharing a largely identical data structure and reporting logic. Maintaining two independent implementations creates duplication and increases maintenance overhead.

This task aims to consolidate both reports into a *single unified report* capable of serving data for both distributors.

h3. *Implementation Notes*

* Identify common fields and metrics across both reports.
* Consolidate report logic into a *single implementation*.
* Introduce a *Distributor identifier/filter* to distinguish between KeHE and UNFI data.
* Ensure existing calculations and report outputs remain consistent with the current reports.

h3. *Acceptance Criteria*

* A single report supports both *KeHE* and *UNFI* data.
* Users can *identify or filter by distributor*.
* Output remains consistent with the existing reports.
* Export functionality (if applicable) continues to work as expected.

08/Apr/26 3:55 PM;624a86b47a3f9e006ab4a185;h1. Price Module Impact Checklist (Cross-Module Validation)

h2. 🔹 Core Rule

{quote}When a *new price is added (new active from date)* → it must reflect correctly across *all related modules and event types*{quote}

----

h1. 1️⃣ Price Module Validation

* New price added with correct *Active From Date*
* No overlapping active dates
* Future date price behaves correctly (not applied before date)
* Price history maintained correctly

----

h1. 2️⃣ Trade Spend Sandbox (TSS) – General

* Updated price reflects in:
** Product Summary
** Event details
* No need for manual refresh (or clearly defined if needed)
* Editing event date updates price dynamically
* Resume draft picks correct price based on date

h3. Date-Based Validation

* If event date *before new price date* → old price used
* If event date *after new price date* → new price used

----

h1. 3️⃣ Non-Promo Event Period

* Same validation as promo:
** Date-based price application works
* Calculation updates correctly:
** Spend
** Revenue
* No mismatch between UI and backend calculation

----

h1. 5️⃣ EDLP Event

EDLP runs across *full year*

Checklist:

* If price changes mid-year:
** System should:
*** Split calculation internally
* Verify:
** Yearly calculation uses correct price for each period
** No flat price applied incorrectly across entire year
* Summary reflects correct blended/updated price

----

h1. 6️⃣ Date Change Impact (Critical)

* Change event start date → price updates
* Change event end date → price recalculates
* Back & forth date change does not break price
* No caching issue (old price showing)

----

h1. 7️⃣ Bulk & Multi-SKU Behavior

* Multiple products → each product uses its own correct price
* Bulk edit does not override price incorrectly
* Different SKUs with different price dates behave correctly

----

h1. 8️⃣ Historical Data Integrity

* Old promos (past dates) should NOT change unexpectedly
* Reports reflect correct historical price
* Editing old promo should not apply future price incorrectly

----

h1. 🔟 UI & UX Validation

* Price clearly visible (no blank/null)
* No “pricing not set” if valid price exists
* Price updates without needing hard refresh (or clearly defined)

----

h1. 1️⃣1️⃣ Edge Cases

* Price active from today (boundary case)
* Multiple price updates in same month
* Missing price for a date → proper message
* Deleted price handling
* Timezone issue (date mismatch)
* Decimal rounding differences
* Price = 0 case
* Same product - Different banner - Different price

column1: TSS - Add Coupon Option
column29:
Can we create a coupon Option? User would enter the Banner, dates, Items, estimated redemption rate and value of coupon and the Lump Sum Fee for adding the Coupon. 

The Estimated value of the coupon would be based on how many Units are projected to sell during the dates selected for the coupon then apply the redemption rate. For example: User Enters 

# Nugget Market 
# $1 off coupon Value 
# 20% Redemption 
# $500 Coupon Fee
# 5 items are selected 

If 80 cases (8 units per case = 640 units) are projected to sell between Jan 1 & Jan 15, and a redemption rate is entered at 20%. It would calculate 128 units * $1 = $128 redemption fee. Plus a a $500 fee across all the items in selected ($100 each)

# *Projected units source for calculation*
#* For {{Estimated Redemption Fee = Projected Units × Redemption Rate × Coupon Value}}, which projected units should be used?
#** promo projected units for selected dates
#** baseline/non-promo projected units
#** both promo + non-promo units
# *Lump sum fee allocation rule*
#* For multi-item coupons, lump sum always be split *equally per selected item* (as in example: $500 / 5 = $100 each), are we correct?
# *Visibility in outputs*
#* In Event Summary / SKU stats / Rollup reports, should coupon values appear:
#** merged into existing spend metrics only, or
#** also as explicit coupon columns/rows?

Once these are confirmed, we can finalize implementation scope and proceed without rework.

* Ensure proper performance handling for large datasets.

*Description:*

# Start creating a new promo in TSS.
# Assign a category/product in Step 2.
# Pause the promo creation (save as draft).
# Update or delete the assigned category/product from the system.
# Resume the promo creation from the draft.

Step 2 should display the updated category/product list or indicate that the assigned items have been removed, allowing the user to reassign. Deleted categories should also be excluded from the category list in step 2.

*Actual Result:*
Step 2 shows a blank state, and the data does not load even after a hard refresh.

# Navigate to *Management>Product Specification>Products* page

# Search for the newly created product.
# Attempt to delete the product.

*Expected Result:* The product should be successfully deleted, and a success pop-up should appear with the message: *“Product deleted successfully“.*
*Actual Result:* The product is not deleted, and an error pop-up appears with the message: *“Selected Products can not be deleted. They are linked to item(s)“.*

+*Sandbox Notes 4/11/25*+

* Search by promo doesn’t work
* Search promos by year doesn’t work
** No way to clear the search when year is entered it displays no record found. User has to refresh button on the search engine to reset

+Add new promo+

* Allow user to click the name of the banner rather than only option to click the chevron

+Step 2 Products+

The stepper doesn’t have option to select Status 

* Status Option should be in step 2 Products
* Can there be a list of options the user can choose in this step?
**  Maybe along the top or the side where user can quickly choose?
** When status is selected only those items appear in the list. 

!image-20250414-130342.png|width=91.66666666666666%,alt="image-20250414-130342.png"!

 +Metrics+

* Need a way to allow user to copy same data down the entire column. Some options could be:
** A double click to auto fill all cells below in same column like in excel
** Or clicking enter automatically takes user to the cell below
** Or check box at the top to indicate auto fil from the top item

+Metrics Entering data+

* Entering data is tricky – when entering values the only way to make the data stick in the field is to click outside of the field.  This is very problematic.  We need to implement a method where the data sticks by hitting enter.

* This is particularly problematic when the user enters the last item. If they don’t click outside of the field and don’t’ realize it, then they select NEXT to generate the promotion, the result is that, that last item didn’t get picked up in the promotion. 

!image-20250414-130359.png|width=100%,alt="image-20250414-130359.png"!

+Multiple Edits:+

* 2 fields are Missing:
** Scan %
** Comment
* Application error after entering information and clicking NEXT
* When user enters the TPR Fee will the fee be divided by the products that are associated with the entry? Example, if there are 5 items and the total fee is $500, it apply $100 to each item?

 Clicking NEXT in after entering data in Metrics doesn’t take user to the results page.

+View and Edit Promo Event Details+

* In this title, change the word “and” to “&”
* The name of the month in the month column doesn’t match the dates.
** Example: Start date = April 20, 2025  End date= April 30, 2025 but the Month says March

!image-20250414-130421.png|width=100%,alt="image-20250414-130421.png"!

* Can’t Edit with any option – Error message says “Promotion not found”
* Add New Event doesn’t work– asks for category but nothing is listed

+Promo Filters+

* None of Promo Filters work

 Please implement auto save draft like in the current version

[BE] Implement multi-tenancy for Brokers
column29:
Implement *multi-tenancy support* for the Brokers module to ensure data isolation and proper access control across different tenants. This will allow multiple organizations or clients to use the system simultaneously while keeping their broker data separate and secure.

h3. Scope of Work:

* Update database schema and queries to support tenant-specific broker data.
* Implement tenant identification and filtering throughout the Brokers module.
* Ensure role-based access and permissions respect tenant boundaries.
* Update existing APIs, services, and UI components to handle multi-tenant context.
* Test data isolation, access control, and edge cases to prevent cross-tenant access.

h3. Acceptance Criteria:

* Broker data is isolated per tenant.
* Only authorized users can access brokers within their tenant.
* Multi-tenancy logic is integrated across APIs and UI.
* Tests validate tenant separation and correct behavior.

column1: [BE] Implement read tables for Market Overview
column29:
Implement *read-only tables* to support the Market Overview functionality, providing users with a consolidated view of market data without allowing direct modifications. This feature will ensure that market insights are displayed efficiently while maintaining data integrity.

h3. Scope of Work:

* Design and implement tables optimized for read-only access to Market Overview data.
* Include relevant fields such as product, category, sales metrics, and other market indicators.
* Ensure efficient querying and pagination for large datasets.
* Integrate tables with the Market Overview UI for display purposes.
* Ensure proper access control so that only authorized users can view the data.
* Implement any necessary indexing or caching to improve performance.

h3. Acceptance Criteria:

* Read-only tables are implemented and populated with relevant market data.
* Users can view Market Overview data without modifying it.
* Queries are optimized for performance with large datasets.
* Access control is enforced for authorized users only.

column1: New Broker Entry
column29:
I had a disappointing meeting with the brokers yesterday.  Essentially, they concluded that the promotional stepper is just too complicated for the team to enter promotions.

After a long discussion we determined that there might be a way to create a new promotional entry system for them, once that’s closer to how they do it today but within Caboodle.  I created the attached sheet to outline how this might work (+New Promo Entry+) and [*this video*|https://zoom.us/clips/share/fiV64x8Fyu7zDjdBXs1LG9MERXhSqO9UKOm_1SJ8124HmbKMSLy-0IBLlLbzQZkPrxKz8JIlRWhLvW9QgBunbk7J.ivk7V3wrMAAO0da4] for you to review on Sunday. Let’s have this as our main discussion on Monday. 

 I forgot to mention in the video

* They don’t need any calculations, so they prefer to enter the discount mechanisms in the new event name. 
* They need to be able to easily copy the event name in multiple rows easily.  If a pull-down option like in excel (select the cell & pull the green box in left bottom corner) that would be ideal or select multiple rows and paste
* Added feature – can they enter comments in the event name with an at @ feature that tags a teammate? Similar to the pipeline?  

I hope this makes sense.  It’s sad that we spent so much time building this the way they directed then it not working for them.  However, the work is not waisted it’s still great for the trade spend sandbox! 

Also attached 3 samples of how users currently enter promotions by Retailer 

* Lazy Acres Promo Grid 
* Berkley Bowl Promo Grid 
* Healthy Living Promo Grid 

Please let me know if this is possible or close to possible and how long this would take.

column1: [BE] Implement User-Based Permission Control Module
column29:
Develop a *User-Based Permission Control Module* to manage and enforce access rights at the individual user level. This will allow fine-grained control over which users can access specific features, actions, or data, independent of their role.

h3. Scope of Work:

* Define a permission structure that can be assigned directly to individual users.
* Implement functionality to check user permissions for all critical operations and UI actions.
* Provide an interface to assign, update, or revoke permissions for each user.
* Integrate permission checks across APIs, services, and UI components.
* Ensure real-time enforcement of permission changes without requiring system restart.
* Include logging and auditing for all permission assignments, revocations, and unauthorized access attempts.

h3. Acceptance Criteria:

* Individual users can be assigned custom permissions.
* Access to features/actions is correctly restricted based on user permissions.
* Permission changes are applied immediately and reflected in the system.
* Audit logs capture all permission modifications and access attempts.
* Unauthorized access is blocked and logged with proper notification.

column29:
The goal here is to implement a status feature for each promo. There should be 2 statuses.  1 Draft, the other Confirmed.  All promos so default to Draft.  User can change to Confirmed.  

If the promotion is in Draft status, it does not push to promotional calendar.  Only if user changes status from Draft to Confirmed does it push to promotional calendar.  

We envision a column on the All Promotions page that has the status listed. Each promotion defaulting to Draft.  If the user selects the check box next to a Promo Name then clicks the Confirmed button, it changes the status from Draft to Confirmed and pushes to the Promotional Calendar.

column29:
*This is for Broker Brands ONLY!* 

For the broker brands the trade spend roll up should pull from the Trade Spend Sandbox. Trade Spend Sandbox was built for broker brands so the promotions they create don’t affect the Promos at a Glance report which is what the brokers use to submit promotions to the retailers. If brands are making promos in trade spend that are only for testing scenarios that means the admin staff would submit to retailers by mistake. That is why we created the sandbox.

Clarification. Trade spend sand box is an enhanced feature that broker brands can opt in and will pay an additional fee.  

For brands that are *not* a part of the brokers we don’t need the trade Spend Sandbox the trade spend roll up report should continue to pull from trade spend.

Let me walk you through a simple workflow to clear up this confusion.

In our system, and actually in most systems, there are two ends: the Frontend and the Backend.

The Frontend is responsible for what you see in your Caboodle system, designing the user interface and ensuring a seamless and intuitive experience. Once the Frontend work is done, users like yourself can interact with the system seamlessly, making the entire application user-friendly.

The Backend, on the other hand, is the engine of the system. It's responsible for the logical implementation of how data is retrieved from or saved into the database, and how data is manipulated. The Backend ensures that the system functions smoothly and efficiently, handling behind-the-scenes operations. 

This ticket specifically pertains to the Backend, indicating that the logical implementation is complete.

Once the Frontend and Backend are integrated, you'll be able to see and use this functionality in the system. 

The collaboration between the Frontend and Backend is crucial – while the Frontend provides the user interface, the Backend powers the functionality, creating a cohesive and user-friendly application.

I hope this clarifies everything.

* User receives an invite to set up their account.
* User enters all info, then clicks Register then the system immediately re-directs them to the Login page, so they enter their login credentials. column1: Investigate why the Price List includes distributors associated while the brand has no distributors.
column29:
!image-20231112-041308.png|width=1733,height=480!

[Live environment] Brand Cocojune has several price lists for the category "Kids Pouches," and the pricing lists have some distributors (red marks) attached, but the brand has no distributors connected.
column136:
12/Nov/23 7:36 PM;63b1b2f415d69a40aa1967b4;[~accountid:712020:bb01de93-d391-4258-af77-200e90d99ec2] , We looked into what was causing this problem. The admin submitted a price list for Brand "Cocojune" on November 2nd, 2023. At the time, our system did not verify whether the brand had a distributor connected or not. When you uploaded a price list at the time, it was just uploaded into the system without any additional checks. 

However, after November 5th, we changed the pricing list import. We implemented a duplicate check as well as a distributor check. Currently, if you enter a distributor ID while uploading a price list, the system checks to see if that distributor has a connection with the specified brand. If it is linked, we permit uploading; otherwise, we do not. 

You are seeing the distributor "KEHE FOB" under the category "Kids Pouches" in the "Cocojune" brand pricing list since the data was uploaded before November 6th. And this verification was not included at the time. 

Now, when uploading a price list from the admin side, do not include the distributor ID if the distributor is not associated with that brand. You are free to leave it blank.  Later, In the brand environment you can add distributors with the price list If you want  by editing price list.

Finally, I have a question: What should we do with the pricing list that includes a distributor that has no connection with the respective brand? Should we connect the distributor to the brand through the brand environment, or should these pricing lists be removed?
